AZ-900 · An API needs processing only when a file arrives. What would you investigate first?
column2:
Event-triggered functions or execution, checking duration, startup, networking, and plan. A permanent VM is optional, and zero cost is not guaranteed.
en/AZ-900/01

column1: AZ-900 · A company needs to configure its own operating system. Which model fits?
column2:
IaaS generally provides that control. PaaS delegates more platform work and may not expose the required settings. Identify control level rather than brand.
en/AZ-900/02

column1: AZ-900 · Three instances are added and users lose sessions. What should be checked?
column2:
Local session state and traffic distribution. Horizontal scaling requires an application designed for multiple instances, not merely additional resources.
en/AZ-900/03

column1: AZ-900 · A Storage URL is public. Can anyone read its contents?
column2:
Not necessarily. Public networking and anonymous access differ; inspect authentication, authorisation, and service configuration.
en/AZ-900/04

column1: AZ-900 · How would you attribute spending to a project?
column2:
Use tags and cost analysis where resource and billing data support them. Cost classification is not permission assignment or an automatic consumption cap.
en/AZ-900/05

column1: AZ-900 · An authenticated user deletes someone else's documents. Must MFA have failed?
column2:
No. Object and operation authorisation failed. MFA does not decide which documents a user may modify.
en/AZ-900/06

column1: AZ-900 · Which service provides recommendations and which observes operations?
column2:
Advisor provides recommendations; Monitor offers operational observation capabilities. Recommendations do not replace actual health evidence.
en/AZ-900/07

column1: AZ-900 · An organisation has slow Internet and a large transfer. What should be compared?
column2:
Network transfers and device options such as Data Box where supported. Consider volume, deadline, security, and validation.
en/AZ-900/08

column1: AZ-900 · Can compliance controls exist while an app remains insecure?
column2:
Yes. Property checks do not prove whole-application security. Inspect permissions, logic, data, and processes as well as policies.
en/AZ-900/09

column1: AZ-900 · How would you demonstrate shared-responsibility understanding?
column2:
List provider and customer responsibilities for a specific workload and explain what changes across VM, PaaS, and SaaS.
en/AZ-900/10

column1: AZ-104 · Reader is removed from a resource but read access remains. What next?
column2:
Inspect inherited assignments, groups, actual identity, and propagation. Granting another role does not remove existing access.
en/AZ-104/01

column1: AZ-104 · An administrator creates Storage but receives 403 listing blobs. What should be checked?
column2:
Authentication method, data role, scope, and service access controls. Management Contributor does not guarantee data access.
en/AZ-104/02

column1: AZ-104 · A VNet-integrated web app remains publicly accessible. Is that contradictory?
column2:
No. App Service VNet integration supports outbound access. Review inbound access, private endpoints, and restrictions separately.
en/AZ-104/03

column1: AZ-104 · All load balancer backends are unhealthy. What should be checked?
column2:
Probe port and expected response, listening process, rules, and configured destination. Existing backends are not necessarily healthy.
en/AZ-104/04

column1: AZ-104 · A peers with B and B with C, but A cannot reach C. Why?
column2:
Peering is not automatically transitive. Design supported connectivity or transit, routes, and security rather than random permission changes.
en/AZ-104/05

column1: AZ-104 · Bicep compiles but Azure denies deployment. What next?
column2:
Check policies, permissions, quotas, names, parameters, and availability. Local compilation does not verify every remote control.
en/AZ-104/06

column1: AZ-104 · A backup succeeds. Can we guarantee a thirty-minute RTO?
column2:
Not without measuring restoration and dependencies. Recover the service rather than merely proving that a copy exists.
en/AZ-104/07

column1: AZ-104 · DNS still returns a public IP after creating a private endpoint. What next?
column2:
Inspect private zones, links, forwarding, and client resolution. Endpoint creation does not automatically configure every consumer.
en/AZ-104/08

column1: AZ-104 · A stopped VM still costs money. What should be distinguished?
column2:
Stopped versus deallocated states and charges for disks and associated resources. Verify state and components before considering cleanup complete.
en/AZ-104/09

column1: AZ-104 · A policy fixes new resources but not old ones. Why might this happen?
column2:
Effects, scope, evaluation, and remediation of existing resources differ. Not every policy modifies or automatically remediates resources.
en/AZ-104/10

column1: AZ-305 · A solution needs zero RPO and one-hour RTO. Are they contradictory?
column2:
Not inherently: data loss and recovery time differ. Validate a concrete solution against both objectives and defined failure scenarios.
en/AZ-305/01

column1: AZ-305 · An application uses JSON and complex transactions. What determines database choice?
column2:
Queries, relationships, transactions, and distribution. JSON transport does not mandate a document database.
en/AZ-305/02

column1: AZ-305 · A small inexperienced team requests AKS for one simple API. What should be discussed?
column2:
Kubernetes requirements, operations, alternatives, and total cost. Do not reject it automatically, but require a reason proportionate to complexity.
en/AZ-305/03

column1: AZ-305 · Regional replication works but data may not leave the country. What is missing?
column2:
Verify replicas, backups, logs, and dependency locations. Resilience does not override residency constraints.
en/AZ-305/04

column1: AZ-305 · The secondary environment lacks secrets and DNS. Is VM replication enough?
column2:
No. Recovery includes identity, configuration, networking, names, and dependencies. Measure the complete path.
en/AZ-305/05

column1: AZ-305 · Caching is proposed to speed reads. What new problem appears?
column2:
Consistency, expiry, and invalidation. Define stale-data tolerance and behaviour when the cache fails or empties.
en/AZ-305/06

column1: AZ-305 · A database migrates overnight while writes continue. What must be defined?
column2:
Initial transfer, supported change capture or synchronisation, cutover window, validation, and rollback. One copy is insufficient.
en/AZ-305/07

column1: AZ-305 · Historical reports slow enrolment. Which alternative should be investigated?
column2:
Separate analytics from transactions and inspect queries and integration. Do not scale everything without understanding the workload.
en/AZ-305/08

column1: AZ-305 · What is missing from a diagram showing only services?
column2:
Requirements, boundaries, identity, data, failures, operations, costs, and validation. Structure alone does not prove suitability.
en/AZ-305/09

column1: AZ-305 · Budget falls while reliability requirements remain. What is the response?
column2:
Compare alternatives with evidence, explain tradeoffs, and negotiate if no validated option exists. Do not promise unchanged objectives automatically.
en/AZ-305/10

column1: AZ-400 · Production rebuilds the artifact after tests. What is the risk?
column2:
Dependencies, tools, or inputs may differ. Promoting the tested, versioned artifact reduces that gap.
en/AZ-400/01

column1: AZ-400 · A migration drops a column and deployment fails. Is image rollback enough?
column2:
No. Schema and data may have changed. Prepare compatibility, migration sequencing, and recovery.
en/AZ-400/02

column1: AZ-400 · A secret was in Git for minutes. What comes first?
column2:
Revoke or rotate it and assess exposure. Removing the commit does not invalidate copied credentials.
en/AZ-400/03

column1: AZ-400 · An external PR runs scripts on an internally connected runner. What matters?
column2:
Trust, isolation, permissions, persistence, and events. PR content can execute code; privileged access needs a secure design.
en/AZ-400/04

column1: AZ-400 · A canary has normal CPU but wrong results. What was missing?
column2:
Functional signals and promotion criteria. Infrastructure health does not prove business correctness.
en/AZ-400/05

column1: AZ-400 · A test passes on its fifth attempt. What next?
column2:
Investigate flakiness and retain evidence. Repeating until green does not make the system reliable.
en/AZ-400/06

column1: AZ-400 · id-token: write exists but Azure rejects login. What should be verified?
column2:
Issuer, subject, audience, federated trust, and configured identity; then authorisation. Workflow permission does not establish all trust.
en/AZ-400/07

column1: AZ-400 · Deployment frequency improves but recovery slows. Is that clearly better?
column2:
Not necessarily. Evaluate speed and stability together using consistent definitions rather than rewarding one metric.
en/AZ-400/08

column1: AZ-400 · An old cache breaks builds. What should be reviewed?
column2:
Keys, inputs, tool versions, and scope. A cache accelerates work; it should not replace correct sources or published artifacts.
en/AZ-400/09

column1: AZ-400 · A postmortem concludes be more careful. What is missing?
column2:
A concrete action, owner, deadline, and verification method. Conclusions should measurably change the system or process.
en/AZ-400/10
